doc.title: Giacomo Gates interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, November 11, 2017 [interview 2 of 2]

chapter: Lyrics and being in the moment
title: Lip syncing joke and reading the poem
summary: Rowe asks about memorized vocalese; Gates jokes about lip syncing and talks about reading his poem as a presentation.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Good words. I was wondering last night, I observed something that these lengthy vocalese things you were doing, you had it all memorized.
You were lip syncing. That answers that question.
I had a cassette player underneath the bandstand.
But then I thought it was interesting because when you went to do your poem about time, which I think is very clever, that you had to read your own work.
But you had memorized all the vocalese from Eddie Jefferson and Jon Hendricks.

And even I mean I read lyrics to songs, they’re in my head. But to read the poem? I don’t know, I never sat down to try to memorize it. It’s just, and I kind of like the — you know I think about that. It looks different when I pick up a piece of paper and read a poem. I was reading a poem.
